problem:
![](images/00/004a94ad9a64973b8e8d3edae709c75f0b76ea1a013d86dbfa87476b85742fc7.png)

Evaluate the line integral
$$
\displaystyle \int_(C)4xyds,
$$
where $C$ is the section of the curve $x = \sqrt{y}$ from $(0, 0)$ to $(\sqrt{2}, 2)$, as shown above.
worked_solution:
Choose the smooth parametrization $x=t$, $y=t^2$, $0\le t\le\sqrt2$. Then $ds=\sqrt{1+4t^2}\,dt$ and $4xy=4t^3$, so

$$
\int_C4xy\,ds=\int_0^{\sqrt2}4t^3\sqrt{1+4t^2}\,dt.
$$

Let $u=1+4t^2$. The bounds become $1$ and $9$, and $4t^3dt=(u-1)du/8$. Therefore

$$
\begin{aligned}
\int_C4xy\,ds&=\frac18\int_1^9(u-1)u^{1/2}\,du\\
&=\frac18\left[\frac25u^{5/2}-\frac23u^{3/2}\right]_1^9
=\frac{149}{15}.
\end{aligned}
$$
